sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: center-lane line patterns and allowed uses, light rail crossings and turns, signs, train lights and pedestrian rules
Look-alike rules from the two-way left turn lane and light rail pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
Along a two-way left turn lane the broken yellow line is the inner line next to the center lane, while the solid yellow line is the outer line. [A01]
Why it matters: group center-lane lines; difficulty three; prereq sec14-F05.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
You may pull into the two-way left turn lane when turning left out of a driveway, but you may not use it to speed up and merge with through traffic. [A01]
Why it matters: group center-lane use; difficulty three; confusable sec14-F07 versus sec14-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A01
Slowing in the two-way left turn lane before a left turn is allowed, while passing or driving straight through in it is not. [A01]
Why it matters: group center-lane use; difficulty two; confusable sec14-F07 versus sec14-F11.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A01
The left turn from a one-way road onto a two-way road ends in the lane just right of the center line and may not be made on a red light. [A01]
Why it matters: group left turns; difficulty two; confusable sec14-F01 versus sec14-F03.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A01
Turning across the METRO tracks is allowed only from signal-controlled turn lanes, and crossing the trackway is allowed only at controlled locations. [A01]
Why it matters: group light rail crossings; difficulty two; confusable sec14-F15 versus sec14-F17.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A02
White headlights mean a light rail train is approaching, while red taillights mean it is moving away from you. [A02]
Why it matters: group train lights; difficulty two; prereq sec14-F31.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A02
A flashing Train Approaching sign warns that a train is coming, while the combined U-turn and left turn sign marks the signal-controlled turns used to cross the tracks. [A02]
Why it matters: group light rail signs; difficulty two; confusable sec14-F23 versus sec14-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A02
A red signal at a light rail crossing means stop, and a red arrow means do not turn. [A02]
Why it matters: group light rail signals; difficulty two; prereq sec14-F27.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A02
Drivers must never stop or park on the tracks, and pedestrians must never walk on them or stand close to them. [A02]
Why it matters: group track safety; difficulty one; confusable sec14-F26 versus sec14-F32.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A02
A quiet train means you cannot rely on hearing it, so you look for flashing headlights and also listen for its bells and horns. [A02]
Why it matters: group train awareness; difficulty two; prereq sec14-F30.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A02
At a light rail crosswalk, children walk their bikes and skateboards across instead of riding them. [A02]
Why it matters: group children; difficulty one; prereq sec14-F36.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0049]
